..
Issued at 212 PM EDT Fri Oct 2 2026

Afternoon RAP analysis and water vapor imagery feature midlevel 
shortwave troughing over eastern Ontario and the Pacific Northwest 
(set to impact our area over the weekend), and ridging over the 
Northern Plains. At the surface, sprawling high pressure is centered 
over southwestern MN, keeping the UP under cool, breezy NW flow. 
Visible satellite shows plenty of lake effect clouds over the NW 
wind belts, and some sprinkles and rain showers continue to be 
reported at times in the far eastern UP. However, model soundings 
show lowering inversion heights over the next few hours as CAA 
weakens, with an increasingly dry airmass overhead. This should 
allow lake clouds to continue to erode. Otherwise, temperatures this 
afternoon are climbing into the mid 50s, and are not expected to 
warm all that much more before sunset. 

With the skies being clear and the antecedent air being quite cool, 
expect temperatures in the areas away from the Great Lakes to drop 
below freezing tonight, with the typical cold spots in the interior 
west potentially dropping down to as low as the lower 20s late 
tonight/early Saturday morning. Therefore, a Freeze Warning remains 
in effect for western and central Upper MI from 10 PM EDT tonight to 
10 AM EDT Saturday. In addition, given that the ridging will create 
nearly calm winds at the sfc, widespread frost is expected across 
the U.P. save the areas north of Houghton. 

Otherwise, expect cooler and more seasonable temperatures this 
weekend into early next week as the aforementioned PacNW troughing 
allows for the development of a Clipper low that moves over the 
Great Lakes Saturday into Sunday. This means that high temperatures 
are projected to range from the mid-50s to mid-60s across the U.P. 
through Monday, while lows drop into the 20s and 30s in the interior 
areas through Monday night (save for Saturday night when clouds and 
rainfall from the Clipper moving through limit lows to the 40s). 

Speaking of the Clipper, while cloud cover from it looks to move 
into the west as early as early Saturday morning, dry air in the 
lower levels looks to prevent anything from reaching the ground 
until at least the late afternoon. However, as the center of the 
Clipper 'clips' (*buh dum tiss*) northern Lake Superior Saturday 
night, CAMs and medium range guidance bring better chances for light 
rainfall across the area Saturday night. While nearly all guidance 
suggests the highest rainfall amounts north of the U.P. Saturday 
night into Sunday morning, the latest REFS run has a general 50 to 
100% chance of at least a tenth of an inch of rain falling over the 
area Saturday night, with the exception being a less than 50% chance 
south of US-2 in Menominee County. While some lake effect sprinkles 
could be seen behind the Clipper during the day Sunday over the 
northwest wind belts, incoming ridging will put an end to it Sunday 
evening. In addition to the rain chances, height falls up to 4 mb/3 
hrs and height rises up to 3 mb/3 hrs ahead of and behind the 
Clipper, respectively, indicate breezy southerly winds preceding the 
Clipper's arrival on Saturday followed by gusty northwest winds 
behind it on Sunday; some northwesterly wind gusts up to 40 mph will 
be possible over the Keweenaw and along the Lake Superior shoreline 
from Marquette County eastward. While the latest NBM shows a 50 to 
70% chance for northwest wind gusts over 40 mph for these areas on 
Sunday, the NBM typically runs hot in these scenarios. Wind gusts 
have thus been knocked back slightly. 

Moving into next week, expect shortwave ridging to keep the area dry 
on Monday while another Clipper brings troughing back to the area 
next Tuesday. However, expect the Clipper's passing to be dry, which 
could increase fire weather concerns ahead of and behind the 
Clipper's passage next week. Moving towards the end of next week, 
medium range guidance slightly differs on the strength of the jet 
stream progging along the U.S./Canada border. Should the jet stream 
be stronger, we could see some light rain chances return as well as 
more 'normal Fall-like' temperatures continuing; if not, then we 
could see a warm-up again to high temperatures returning to the 60s 
across most of the area.
